children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures closed stronger on Monday, continuing their see-saw track record over the last month of trading.
Comparable oils Significant increases in the Chicago soy complex and European rapeseed spilled over into canola. However, Malaysian palm oil was lower on the day.
Crude oil was down hard, on what's believed to be a selloff to reduce its long position.
Slow harvest The Prairie harvest remained well behind its average pace, especially in Alberta.
However, a spate of plus 20-degree weather and no rain over the next few day will be helpful to farmers.
Other factors The November canola contract pushed above its major moving averages, further underpinning its values.
The Canadian dollar was backtracking on Monday afternoon, with the loonie at 71.24 U.S. cents, compared to Friday's close of 71.42.
Contracts There were 50,142 canola contracts traded on Monday, compared to 44,990 on Friday. Spreading accounted for 25,736 contracts traded.
